content.text:
The drawing is a PROTAC-type molecule: a sunitinib-like warhead, a piperazine-containing linker, and a pomalidomide-type cereblon ligand.

**Warhead (left).** This is a 5-fluoro-1-methyl-2-oxindole with an exocyclic double bond at C3 to a CH. That CH attaches to a pyrrole carrying two methyl groups and a carboxamide.
- Oxindole: CN1C(=O)C(=Cc2...)c3cc(F)ccc13
- Pyrrole: c2[nH]c(C)c(C(=O)N...)c2C, with the CH attached at C5, the NH at position 1, C4 carrying the methyl next to the amide-bearing C3, and C2 carrying a methyl.

**Linker.**
- The amide NH connects through a propyl chain, NCCC, to a piperazine nitrogen.
- The other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2C(=O)NH.
- That NH continues through a pentyl chain, (CH2)5, to an NH on the aryl ring.

**Cereblon ligand (right).** The aryl NH sits on the 4-position of a phthalimide, and the imide nitrogen carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

**Stereochemistry.** The oxindole double bond is drawn with a defined geometry. In sunitinib the Z configuration places the pyrrole NH on the same side as the oxindole C=O. In the drawing, the oxindole C3 has the aromatic ring on its left side, and the CH attached to the pyrrole lies to the left. The pyrrole NH points down, toward the C2 carbonyl side, so this matches the Z form. The glutarimide stereocentre is drawn plain, so it gets no stereo label.

**Writing the SMILES for Z.** At C3, the substituents are C2 (the C=O) and C3a (aromatic). On the CH, the substituents are the pyrrole and H. The pyrrole should be on the same side as C2(=O), which gives:
O=C1N(C)c2ccc(F)cc2/C1=C\c1[nH]c(C)c(C(=O)N...)c1C

Check of the ring-closure form: the atom before C1 in "c2/C1=C\c1" is the aromatic carbon c2, so "/C1" puts the aromatic carbon on one side. With "/C1=C\c", the aromatic carbon (written before, with "/") and the pyrrole (written after, with "\") are on the same side. That would place the pyrrole on the aromatic side, which is E. To get Z, I use "/C1=C/c" instead, which puts the pyrrole opposite the aromatic carbon and therefore on the C=O side.

Full SMILES:
O=C1N(C)c2ccc(F)cc2/C1=C/c1[nH]c(C)c(C(=O)NCCCN2CCN(CC(=O)NCCCCCNc3cccc4c3C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C4=O)CC2)c1C

SMILES: O=C1N(C)c2ccc(F)cc2/C1=C/c1[nH]c(C)c(C(=O)NCCCN2CCN(CC(=O)NCCCCCNc3cccc4c3C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C4=O)CC2)c1C
